items.prompt: What is the dark area where light is blocked called?

options.label: A shadow
options.feedback: Correct. A shadow is the dark area on a surface where light from a source is blocked.

options.label: A shade
options.feedback: Shade is the three-dimensional volume behind an object, not the dark area on a surface.

options.label: A silhouette
options.feedback: A silhouette is the cross-section shape of a shadow, but it is not what the dark area itself is called.

options.label: A penumbra
options.feedback: A penumbra is a specific part of a shadow from an extended source, not the general name for the dark area.

items.ok_line: A shadow is the dark patch where light is blocked.
items.ko_line: Pick the name for the dark area itself.
items.exp_text: A shadow is a two-dimensional dark area on a surface. Shade is the three-dimensional space behind an object with light in front.

items.prompt: What kind of light source produces an umbra without a penumbra?

options.label: An extended source
options.feedback: An extended source produces umbra, penumbra, and antumbra, not only an umbra.

options.label: A point source
options.feedback: Correct. A point source casts only the simple umbra with no penumbra.

options.label: A diffuse source
options.feedback: Diffuse lighting softens shadows, but it is not what produces a single umbra.

options.label: The Sun
options.feedback: The Sun is an extended source, so it casts both umbra and penumbra.

items.ok_line: A point source gives just a plain umbra.
items.ko_line: Think of a single tiny light.
items.exp_text: A point source of light is small and casts only a simple shadow called the umbra. Extended sources divide the shadow into umbra, penumbra, and antumbra.

items.prompt: Which part of a shadow receives no direct light from any part of the light source?

options.label: The penumbra
options.feedback: The penumbra receives light from some parts of the source, so it is not fully dark.

options.label: The antumbra
options.feedback: The antumbra is a zone beyond the umbra and is not the part with no direct light.

options.label: The umbra
options.feedback: Correct. The umbra region gets no light from any part of the source, making it the darkest.

options.label: The silhouette
options.feedback: A silhouette is the shape of the shadow, not a region of darkness within it.

items.ok_line: The umbra is the fully dark core.
items.ko_line: Only one part is completely light-free.
items.exp_text: The umbra does not receive any direct light from any part of the light source, so it is the darkest region. A viewer in it cannot see any part of the source.

items.prompt: What happens to a shadow when the light source becomes wider?

options.label: It becomes sharper
options.feedback: A wider source makes the shadow more blurred, not sharper.

options.label: It becomes darker
options.feedback: A wider source lets more light around the edges, reducing sharpness and contrast, not increasing darkness.

options.label: It disappears completely
options.feedback: A wider source blurs the edges, but the shadow does not vanish unless the source is very diffuse.

options.label: It becomes more blurred
options.feedback: Correct. The wider the light source, the more blurred the shadow becomes.

items.ok_line: A wider light blurs the shadow edges.
items.exp_text: With a wider or extended light source, light comes from many directions, so the shadow's edges get blurred. A point source, in contrast, gives a crisp umbra only.

items.prompt: What is it called when two overlapping penumbras appear to merge?

options.label: The shadow blister effect
options.feedback: Correct. When two penumbras overlap, the shadows seem to attract and merge, which is the shadow blister effect.

options.label: Rayleigh scattering
options.feedback: Rayleigh scattering makes shadows bluish, but it does not cause merging.

options.label: A lunar eclipse
options.feedback: A lunar eclipse is Earth's shadow on the Moon, not a merging of penumbras.

options.label: Crepuscular rays
options.feedback: Crepuscular rays are beams of light, not overlapping shadows.

items.ok_line: Overlapping penumbras merge in the blister effect.
items.ko_line: This is about shadows, not light beams.
items.exp_text: When two penumbras overlap, the shadows appear to attract each other and merge, an effect called the shadow blister effect. It happens with extended sources.

items.prompt: Under what lighting condition does an overcast sky produce almost no visible shadows?

options.label: When the sun is a point source
options.feedback: The Sun is never a point source; also overcast skies are diffuse, not point-like.

options.label: When there are multiple light sources
options.feedback: Multiple sources create several shadows, not none.

options.label: When the lighting is diffuse
options.feedback: Correct. The more diffuse the lighting, the softer and more indistinct the shadows, until they disappear.

options.label: When the object is far from the surface
options.feedback: A far object makes a larger and blurred shadow, but it still exists.

items.exp_text: An overcast sky provides very diffuse light, so shadows become soft and indistinct and may disappear. Diffuse lighting spreads light from many directions.

items.prompt: What color tinge does a daytime shadow cast by an opaque object in sunlight have?

options.label: Red
options.feedback: Red tint comes from other scattering conditions, not from Rayleigh scattering in the atmosphere.

options.label: Bluish
options.feedback: Correct. Rayleigh scattering makes the sky blue, and this ambient blue light fills the shadow, giving it a bluish tinge.

options.label: Green
options.feedback: Green is not the color from Rayleigh scattering.

options.label: Black only
options.feedback: A shadow is never purely black in open air because ambient light from the sky fills it.

items.ok_line: Daytime shadows look bluish due to the sky.
items.ko_line: The sky's blue light colors the shadow.
items.exp_text: Rayleigh scattering makes the sky blue. The object blocks the sun's direct light but not the blue sky light, so the shadow appears bluish.

options.label: A shadow caused by rain droplets
options.feedback: Rain shadows are not light shadows; they are dry regions, not dark areas.

options.label: A shadow seen in fog
options.feedback: A fog shadow is a volumetric light shadow, not a dry region.

options.label: An acoustic shadow
options.feedback: An acoustic shadow is a blocked sound area, not a rain effect.

options.label: A dry area beyond a mountain range
options.feedback: Correct. A rain shadow is a dry area on the leeward side of a mountain range where clouds are blocked.

items.ok_line: A rain shadow is a dry zone behind mountains.
items.ko_line: This is about weather, not light.
items.exp_text: A rain shadow is a dry area that is beyond a mountain range with respect to the prevailing wind, because the elevated terrain blocks rainclouds from entering.

items.prompt: What happens to a shadow's size when the surface it falls on is farther from the object?

options.label: It becomes larger
options.feedback: Correct. The farther the projection surface, the larger the silhouette, proportionally.

options.label: It becomes smaller
options.feedback: The shadow grows, not shrinks, with distance.

options.label: It stays the same size
options.feedback: The size changes because light rays spread out with distance.

options.label: It disappears
options.feedback: The shadow does not vanish; it gets larger and more blurred.

items.ok_line: A farther surface makes a bigger shadow.
items.exp_text: The distance from the object to the projection surface is proportional to the silhouette size. Farther away, the shadow expands.

items.prompt: What is the name for the fear of shadows?

options.label: Claustrophobia
options.feedback: Claustrophobia is the fear of enclosed spaces, not shadows.

options.label: Arachnophobia
options.feedback: Arachnophobia is the fear of spiders.

options.label: Sciophobia
options.feedback: Correct. The fear of shadows is called sciophobia or sciaphobia.

options.label: Nyctophobia
options.feedback: Nyctophobia is the fear of night or darkness, not of shadows specifically.

items.ok_line: Sciophobia is the fear of shadows.
items.ko_line: This is about shadows, not other fears.
items.exp_text: The name for the fear of shadows is sciophobia or sciaphobia. It is a specific phobia related to shadows.
